title: Lantern Works x Redwood - Hybrid GPU Partner Interop Discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery focused on Lantern Works' hybrid GPU offering and integration points with Redwood. Main themes: private VPC connectivity, dedicated capacity vs hosted fallbacks, billing/throughput models, and pilot benchmarking. Customer requested security docs, pricing ballpark, and a short pilot plan. SE to run quick perf benchmarks and share config suggestions.
action_items: Maya Thompson - Share partner intro deck and high-level pricing sheet by 2026-04-15
Connor Reed - Run a 1hr perf benchmark with Lantern sample payloads and share results by 2026-04-20
Tom Becker (Customer) - Send sample traffic profile and a representative prompt corpus by 2026-04-16
next_steps: Schedule technical deep dive (SE-led) next week
Provision test tokens for Lantern Works staging VPC
Share SOC2 + network architecture docs link
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-13
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya T (Redwood AE), Connor R (Redwood SE), Priya R (Redwood SE), Alicia G (Lantern Head of AI), Tom B (Lantern Cloud Architect), Samir K (Lantern CTO), Jae P (Lantern Infra)

Summary (auto): quick partner sync, scope integration and pilot, identify security and connectivity constraints, agree next steps for benchmarks and docs.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:03] Alicia (Lantern): hey, thanks. Alicia here, head of ai at Lantern Works.
[00:05] Tom (Lantern): Tom Becker, cloud architect, on the call.
[00:08] Samir (Lantern): Samir, CTO.
[00:10] Jae (Lantern): Jae, infra lead.
[00:12] Maya (Redwood): awesome. connor and priya from our solutions eng team--they'll do the deep tech coverage. i'll run the agenda.
[00:20] Connor (Redwood): hi all, quick note, if transcription bot garbles any product names forgive us, sometimes the kv cache becomes 'key vish' in the logs.
[00:28] Tom (Lantern): ha, noted. ok so high level: lantern runs a hybrid offering — customers can run inference on our on-prem racks or on cloud burst. we're exploring a partner integration so we can surface redwood-managed models as endpoints or route traffic to redwood when customers want hosted fallback.
[00:45] Maya (Redwood): great. are you thinking of reseller/channel partnership or deeper infra integration?
[00:52] Alicia (Lantern): both. initially channel: we want to onboard 2 pilot customers where we offer Redwood models via our console. longer term, potentially an onramp where we run redwood runtime on our racks or do peering.
[01:10] Connor (Redwood): ok, good. can you share current infra? like k8s, bare metal, what gpus, what networking?
[01:18] Jae (Lantern): mostly bare-metal DGX-ish style nodes, mix of A100 and a few H100s, on a private VLAN. we run a custom orchestrator (not full k8s), and we use an internal secrets manager and a keyvault. we do SAML SSO and have SOC2 type 2.
[01:36] Connor (Redwood): perfect, that maps well. there are two main integration patterns we recommend: 1) hosted integration — your console calls Redwood hosted API with per-tenant tokens, good for fast time to market; 2) private/dedicated — either colocate Redwood private runtime in your VPC or run our private control plane and route inference to your dedicated gpu pools. tradeoffs are cost, latency, and operational complexity.
[01:58] Samir (Lantern): latency is big for some customers. sub-100ms per token is ideal for live apps, but our batch jobs can tolerate higher. what's redwood's sweet spot?
[02:08] Connor (Redwood): depends on model & sequence length. for smaller autoregressive models hosted in our low-latency tier we hit ~40-80ms for short 32-token responses on optimized kernels. for larger contexts or on V100/A100 older nodes you may see 150-300ms. we do continuous batching, prefix kv caching and optimized kernels, but on bare metal in your data center latency will also depend on network hops.
[02:36] Tom (Lantern): okay, and cost? customers will ask. do you have a pricing band for dedicated GPU pools vs hosted?
[02:44] Maya (Redwood): we'll share a ballpark pricing sheet — hosted is unit-based per-token + embedding units, dedicated is more of a reserved commit with monthly pricing and optional burst. for reseller deals we can discuss rev-share. i'll attach a high-level sheet after call.
[02:59] Alicia (Lantern): security questions — we need audit logs, KMS integration, HSM compatibility, and data residency. can we get SOC2 and network diagrams?
[03:08] Priya (Redwood): yes, we have SOC2 docs, we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments, and we can do a VPC peering model. audit logs and per-request tracing are available in our console. we can also generate token-level cost/latency breakdowns for customers.
[03:26] Jae (Lantern): about VPC peering — we often operate in air-gapped sites for regulated customers. is an on-prem package available?
[03:34] Connor (Redwood): we do offer an on-prem private package that runs behind customer firewalls. it requires some minimal control-plane reachability for telemetry unless you opt for fully air-gapped install. that path has longer lead times and a different licensing model.
[03:50] Samir (Lantern): lead times? how long to get on-prem up and running?
[03:54] Maya (Redwood): with pre-reqs in place 6-10 weeks typical; fully air-gapped can be 12+ weeks. hosted or VPC-peering pilots can spin up in days to a couple weeks.
[04:06] Alicia (Lantern): for the pilot we want to test both latency-critical flows and batch workloads. can you support benchmark scripts against both hosted and a dedicated instance?
[04:16] Connor (Redwood): yes. we can run perf benchmarks, and we recommend bringing a representative prompt corpus and traffic pattern. we'll run the tests on a dedicated node config closest to yours — we can also run a hosted baseline for comparison.
[04:30] Tom (Lantern): our orchestration uses an internal queuing pattern and replays — some things to be mindful of when benchmarking: tokenization differences, input chunking. do you have a recommended harness?
[04:40] Priya (Redwood): we have a benchmarking harness and a template repo. we'll share the link. it includes tokenization utilities, payload simulators, and a spreadsheet to collect latency/throughput numbers.
[04:52] Alicia (Lantern): great. integration specifics: how do we authenticate calls from our console to Redwood?
[04:57] Maya (Redwood): for hosted: api keys with per-tenant scopes; for private/dedicated: mutual TLS or mTLS plus short-lived tokens and optional SAML integration for user-level auth. we also have RBAC support in the console.
[05:12] Jae (Lantern): we need to ensure secrets flow through our vault and not be in plaintext anywhere. KMS integration ok?
[05:17] Priya (Redwood): yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for private deployments. for hosted we can integrate with external KMS using an HSM-backed keywrap for extra protections.
[05:28] Alicia (Lantern): any constraints on models? we want to offer LLMs and embeddings; some customers want quantized smaller models for cost reasons.
[05:36] Connor (Redwood): we support a model catalog — both larger and quantized variants. quantization can reduce memory and cost but may impact output quality for some tasks. we can recommend quantization profiles based on workload. for embeddings we have dedicated embed endpoints that scale differently.
[05:55] Tom (Lantern): curious about routing — if a customer is on Lantern on-prem but we need to failover to Redwood hosted due to capacity, is that automatic?
[06:03] Maya (Redwood): yes, we have smart routing and fallback policies. requests can be routed by latency/cost/availability. automatic fallback to compatible model variants is possible. we can surface a canary policy in the console to control that.
[06:20] Samir (Lantern): excellent. competitor question: some customers ask about Apex Cloud's similar offering, how are you different?
[06:26] Connor (Redwood): two main diffs: production-first runtime with detailed unit economics and a unified API across hosted/dedicated/private. plus our tooling for batching/caching and rollouts is more opinionated for production.
[06:41] Jae (Lantern): ok, let's outline pilot scope. we propose: 1) channel pilot — integrate Redwood hosted API into Lantern console for two customers for 4 weeks; 2) performance pilot — run dedicated-reserved instance tests with our sample prompts for 2 weeks.
[06:58] Maya (Redwood): sounds reasonable. for the channel pilot we can provision test tokens and limits; for the dedicated perf pilot we'll set a small reserved pool with telemetry access.
[07:10] Alicia (Lantern): timeline — we'd like to start the channel pilot in early May. is that realistic?
[07:14] Maya (Redwood): yes, if we get the sample corpus and reqs by next Friday we can ramp in 2-3 weeks.
[07:21] Tom (Lantern): action for us: we'll share traffic profile and sample prompts; also we'll identify two pilot customers and confirm legal minimal requirements.
[07:32] Connor (Redwood): i'll need the sample sequences and target p99/p50 latency requirements. i'll also run an initial run on our hosted baseline, then the dedicated config.
[07:44] Maya (Redwood): i'll share partner deck and pricing, also SOC2 and network diagrams.
[07:49] Alicia (Lantern): excellent. a few nitty gritty questions before we close: what about rate limits and DDoS protections?
[07:56] Priya (Redwood): we have global rate limiting tiers and edge protections; for dedicated pools you can get custom limits. we also support per-tenant quotas and throttling.
[08:07] Jae (Lantern): how about logging retention — some customers need 7+ years for audit.
[08:12] Maya (Redwood): default logs retention is 90 days in hosted, but for enterprise/dedicated we can negotiate longer retention as part of the contract and also exportable audit logs to your S3.
[08:25] Samir (Lantern): good. any integrations needed on our side for observability? we use prometheus and grafana.
[08:31] Connor (Redwood): we have tracing hooks and can push metrics to prometheus endpoints or expose them via our agent. we'll share the agent doc.
[08:42] Tom (Lantern): noted. last item: licensing for reselling and revenue share — high level?
[08:48] Maya (Redwood): reseller rev-share is negotiable; we typically structure partner discounts tied to committed volumes and have an introducer fee for initial pilots. legal can follow up with a partner MSA draft.
[09:02] Alicia (Lantern): ok great. thanks everyone. let's recap next steps.
[09:07] Maya (Redwood): recap: we'll share partner deck, pricing ballpark, SOC2 and network diagrams; we'll provision test tokens for channel pilot; Connor will run perf benchmarks after Lantern shares corpus and traffic; Lantern to identify pilots and send sample payloads. schedule se-led deep dive next week.
[09:28] Tom (Lantern): we'll target sending the samples by 2026-04-16.
[09:34] Connor (Redwood): i'll aim to run the first hosted baseline by 2026-04-18 and dedicated perf run by 2026-04-20.
[09:43] Maya (Redwood): perfect. thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[09:47] Alicia (Lantern): thanks, bye.

References shared (in chat):
- Partner intro deck: https://redwood.example.com/partners/lantern-intro-deck

Notes about transcription: occasional speaker label confusion, some acronyms were mis-heard (e.g., HSM as 'h-s-m' or 'h-s-mm'), product names sometimes simplified.
notes: Pilot plan split: channel hosted pilot + dedicated perf run. Customer needs SOC2, KMS + audit logs. Next: exchange sample corpus and run benchmarks.
